description: Scripted event streams run through the same strategy in Python and Rust (ADR 008). events are wire Messages; intents carry the ts_init they were submitted at; fills are wire Trades; observations are what contract_probe read from its context on each hook.

scenarios.name: contract_probe_mixed_stream
scenarios.description: Every hook and context capability: start intent processed with the first event, on_fill intent processed with the next event, busy gating, all four order types, ts_init != ts_event (event 4), instrument lookup (lot 75, tick 0.05), cash, and an on_stop intent that is never executed.

scenarios.name: contract_probe_unknown_instrument
scenarios.description: Instrument lookup misses: the probe falls back to lot 1 and tick 0.01; a trade tick while busy submits nothing.

scenarios.name: buy_and_hold
scenarios.description: Reference BuyAndHold: one market buy on the first bar.

scenarios.name: sma_crossover
scenarios.description: Reference SmaCrossover (fast 2, slow 3): sell on the cross down at bar 5, buy on the cross up at bar 8. It trades crosses, not positions, so it sells while flat.

scenarios.name: contract_probe_fill_time_and_ts_init
scenarios.description: Two events share ts_init 100, so the second order (the on_fill protective stop) fills at max(order ts 100, previous fill ts 100 + 1) = 101; the trade tick with ts_event 200 != ts_init 210 submits a stop buy that is stamped ts_init 210 (and the clock reads 210), not 200. Bar events carry ts_event 95 != ts_init 100 likewise.

scenarios.name: contract_probe_fill_costs
scenarios.description: Non-zero fill costs (flat 0.5 + 625 bps of the notional): every fill carries cost = 0.5 + q*p*625/10000, a buy debits q*p + cost, a sell credits q*p - cost. Expected values derived by hand from ADR 008.
